package_info.package_versions: All versions distributed via online panels and third-party websites
package_info.why_malicious: The package is designed to lock the device screen using SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, abuse accessibility and notification services, and display a persistent ransom note, coercing users to pay to regain access. It employs obfuscation and loads its main payload in memory to evade detection.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on app launch or after installation)
execution_context.file_location: Main application code (e.g., MainActivity.java or equivalent entry point)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code requests SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW permission and overlays a ransom note view on top of all other UI elements, blocking user interaction and access to the device.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate apps rarely use SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW to block all user input and display persistent, non-dismissible overlays.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps use this permission for brief system alerts or error messages, not to lock the entire device and demand ransom.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Chat heads in messaging apps or accessibility overlays for visually impaired users.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after initial execution or on specific event)
execution_context.file_location: Obfuscated main payload in memory, invoked via gvmthHtyN.XoqF()

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: gvmthHtyN.XoqF(appObj, configurations); // Obfuscated method call to trigger main payload
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code invokes an obfuscated method to load and execute the main ransomware payload from memory, enabling further malicious actions such as screen locking and ransom note display.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated method names and in-memory payload loading are common techniques to evade static analysis and detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps do not obfuscate core logic to this extent or load main functionality dynamically from memory.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some DRM or anti-tamper solutions may use obfuscation, but not for user-facing core logic.
key_indicators: Lack of descriptive code in visible files

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code abuses accessibility services to monitor for attempts to dismiss the overlay and immediately re-displays the ransom note, ensuring persistent lockout.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessibility services are being used to enforce malicious UI behavior and prevent user recovery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Accessibility services are intended to help users with disabilities, not to enforce malicious overlays.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Accessibility features for screen readers or input assistance.
key_indicators: Accessibility event monitoring for system dialogs

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code abuses notification services to suppress or override legitimate system notifications, further preventing the user from receiving help or system alerts.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Suppressing system notifications is a technique to prevent user awareness and hinder recovery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Notification listeners are meant for user convenience, not to suppress critical system alerts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Notification management apps, but not for suppressing security or system notifications.

attack_chain.action: App is installed and requests SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, accessibility, and notification permissions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Preparation for device lockout and ransom note display

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated main payload is loaded and executed in memory.
Ransom note overlay is displayed, blocking all user input and access.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is locked out and prompted to pay ransom

attack_chain.action: Accessibility and notification services are abused to prevent overlay dismissal and suppress system alerts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistent lockout and reduced chance of user recovery

behavioral_signatures: Requesting SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, accessibility, and notification permissions in combination
Persistent, non-dismissible overlays that block all user input
Obfuscated code with meaningless class and method names
Dynamic loading and execution of main payload from memory
file_indicators: APK files with obfuscated class/method names
Presence of classes like gvmthHtyN or methods like XoqF
Unusual use of accessibility and notification service handlers
network_indicators: May contact C2 servers for ransom payment instructions (not explicitly mentioned in report, but typical for ransomware)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps requesting SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, accessibility, and notification permissions together. Flag apps that display persistent overlays blocking all input. Analyze APKs for obfuscated code and dynamic payload loading. Detect suppression of system notifications and abuse of accessibility events to enforce overlays. Use behavioral analysis to identify apps that lock the screen and demand ransom.
